It's a difficult thing to explain and it goes much further than just how people behave. I'd suggest going to a place in Asia for a bit to see how different it is. I know in China you see huge differences from how you pay your bill at a restaurant, to the fact people hold hands as a sign of friendship (you can see two old guys holding hands walking down the street some times), etc.

People have more than one culture. They have their local culture, which is a subset of where they live. If you ever hear people talk about how the people in the north/south/east/west/etc are nicer/ruder/etc than that's what they're talking about. Then you have the country's culture, generally focused on food, traditional and modern arts, technology, societal focuses (France values food, fine arts, etc, Germany historically has not been fond of those and more focused on war and technology). On top of that, you have a larger culture. Example is Americans, Europeans, etc have a culture that revolves around capitalism, buying things, etc.

If you are fortunate enough to see different parts of the world, you realize that people think and behave completely differently. People in China have limited individuality, yet people in Japan will get really upset if you take their individuality away. Those are the types of things that form a culture. Understanding your own culture is definitely a type of "can't see the forest from the trees" type of situation, as well as being so absorbed in it and not being able to escape it that you can't recognize it because it's second nature to you.

I understand why why there's confusion over German and Iranian cultures, though. The thing is, you're looking at cultures between different countries and then assuming they are the same difference between cultures between different regions. What's happening is not a German and Iranian culture mixing, but Western and Middle Eastern cultures mixing. It is definitely possible to mix some of them, but try and compare a culture like Asian to Western to Middle Eastern to African and judge by then.
